title: Critique Cred onboarding vs Jupiter
persona: Priya, senior designer on Jupiter onboarding
scenario: Your design lead saw Cred's onboarding flow and asked, ‘why doesn't ours feel like that?’ You need a structured critique: what Cred does well, what's actually a Cred-specific brand move that wouldn't transplant, and what 2 things from Cred we should steal AND 1 trap we'd fall into if we copy too much. Design review is on Friday.
badOutput: Cred has a polished onboarding with strong copy and animations. Jupiter has a friendly onboarding focused on clarity. Both are good but cater to different audiences. Cred is for premium users, Jupiter for mass market.

hints.title: Force a separation
hints.body: ‘Separate Cred's transferable patterns from Cred's brand-specific moves.’ Without this, designers cargo-cult the brand layer and miss the actual UX.

hints.title: Surface a trap
hints.body: Demand one trap, ‘what we'd break if we copied this’. Critique without traps is flattery.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a critique, not a comparison.
Anchor the surface, onboarding flow, not the whole product.
Name both products and the brand context, fintech onboarding.
Reference the audience and deadline, design review on Friday.
Force the separation, transferable vs brand-specific.
Demand a trap, what we'd break if we copy too much.
Lock the count, 2 things to steal. Specificity beats a flat list.
Lock 1 trap. The asymmetry, 2 steals + 1 trap, forces real critique.
Specify the structure, transferable vs brand-specific in a table.
Anchor the critique to specific screens or steps, not vibes.

tipIfLow: Critique without separation becomes flattery. The unlock is forcing transferable vs brand-specific, plus one trap. Without traps, design teams cargo-cult competitor brand moves and break their own product.
goldPrompt: You're a design-critique partner. I'm Priya, senior designer on Jupiter onboarding. Lead asked: 'why doesn't ours feel like Cred's?' Output 4 sections: (1) What Cred onboarding does well — 4 patterns with screen references, (2) Cred's brand-specific moves that won't transplant — argue why each is brand-coupled, (3) The 2 transferable patterns to steal, (4) ONE trap we'd fall into if we copied too much. Refuse to praise without naming a transferable mechanism. Audience: design review Friday.
